details:
**Donald Tusk**
Leader of the Civic Platform party who became Poland's Prime Minister again in December 2023, ending eight years of Law and Justice rule. He had previously been prime minister from 2007 to 2014 and President of the European Council from 2014 to 2019.

**Law and Justice (PiS)**
Poland's right-wing, nationalist-conservative party, which governed from 2015 until it lost its parliamentary majority in the October 2023 election. Its time in power was marked by fights with the EU over judicial independence and the rule of law.

**Jarosław Kaczyński**
Longtime leader of Law and Justice and the most powerful figure in Polish politics during its time in government. He is the twin brother of former president Lech Kaczyński, who died in the Smolensk crash.

**Civic Platform**
Poland's main centrist, pro-EU party and the chief rival of Law and Justice, led by Donald Tusk. It attacked the PiS government over the 2023 visa scandal.

**Smolensk air disaster**
The 2010 crash of a Polish Air Force plane near Smolensk, Russia, which killed 96 people, including President Lech Kaczyński and many members of parliament and senior officials. Law and Justice promoted conspiracy theories about the crash and accused Tusk of failing to investigate it properly, which deepened the country's political divisions.

**Paweł Adamowicz**
The liberal mayor of Gdańsk, who was fatally stabbed on stage at a charity event in January 2019. His murder was widely seen as a result of Poland's bitter political polarization.

**NATO Article 4 and Russian drones**
In September 2025, Russian drones crossed into Polish airspace and some were shot down. Prime Minister Tusk invoked Article 4 of the NATO treaty, which calls for allied consultations when a member feels threatened.

**Karol Nawrocki**
The Law and Justice–backed historian who won Poland's 2025 presidential election. During the campaign, he used pouch tobacco (snus) on camera during a debate and faced allegations that he had helped arrange prostitutes while working as a security guard at the Grand Hotel in Sopot.

**"Not One More" protests and Izabela**
The "Not One More" protests broke out in 2021 after a pregnant woman named Izabela died of sepsis in a hospital. Doctors had delayed treatment because of Poland's near-total abortion ban.

**"LGBT-Free Zones"**
Many Polish towns and regions under PiS influence declared themselves "LGBT-free zones," and some pride marches were banned or attacked. The EU condemned the zones and withheld some funding in response.

**Belarus border wall**
In January 2022, Poland began building a wall along its border with Belarus. It was a response to a migrant crisis that Belarus's regime was accused of engineering by flying in migrants and pushing them toward the EU border.

**Grzegorz Braun's menorah incident**
In December 2023, far-right member of parliament Grzegorz Braun used a fire extinguisher to put out a Hanukkah menorah in the Sejm (the Polish parliament), injuring a woman. The act was widely condemned as antisemitic.

**Visa scandal**
The 2023 "cash-for-visas" scandal, in which officials of the PiS-led government were accused of selling or illegally issuing visas to migrants. It was a major issue for Civic Platform during the 2023 election campaign.

**Disputes with Ukraine**
In 2023, Poland and Ukraine clashed over grain imports and over a blockade of the border by Polish truckers, who objected to competition from Ukrainian haulers. During the grain dispute, the PiS government announced it would stop sending weapons to Ukraine.

**Olga Tokarczuk and Kler**
Conservatives threatened Olga Tokarczuk, the Polish novelist whose book Flights won the 2018 Man Booker International Prize. They also tried to suppress Kler, a 2018 film critical of the Catholic clergy.
